study_identification.title: Distinct Neurodevelopmental Patterns and Intermediate Integration-Based Predictive Modeling in Autism Spectral Disorder

study_characteristics.study_objective: To characterize the distinct developmental patterns of cortical morphology in individuals with ASD, investigate the important neural biomarkers for ASD diagnostics, and propose a deep-learning workflow that combined graph convolutional networks with lowrank multi-model tensor fusion (LMFGCN) for ASD prediction.

quality_checking_detail.answer: The quality control was assessed by inspecting the image and the cortical reconstructed results across individual brains by two independent reviewers (YL.W. and S.T.). To enhance the accuracy of QA and to investigate the reasons of image exclusion, we also use quality control software for MRI data (MRIQC) to compute image quality metrics for each dataset. In ABIDE-I, 238 participants were excluded. In ABIDE-II, 243 participants were excluded. In KQJH, 59 participants were excluded.

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: ComBat harmonization was used to control for confounding effect of age, sex, and site effects.

response_variable.answer: Cortical thickness (CT), surface area (SA), and gray matter volume (GV)

predictor_effects.answer: Fixed effects for sex and site. Smoothing function for age.

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The paper mentions using GAMLSS to model heteroskedasticity and non-gaussian distributions, and ComBat for site effects, but a comprehensive evaluation of how well nuisance structures are handled is not presented.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: The approach of estimating mean and standard deviation from the residuals won’t work for brain development over the lifespan, such as heteroskedastic and non-gaussian models. Generalized additive models for location, scale and shape (GAMLSS) can be used to model multi-parameter distributions... we then used ComBat (github.com/ Jfortin1/ComBatHarmonization), a batch-effect correction tool, to control for confounding effect of age, sex, and site effects.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The paper explicitly states that the data was split into a 70% training set and a 30% test set, and the models were evaluated on the training set.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: First, all data was split into 70% train dataset and 30% test dataset...Then, we compared each models in the training set and then validate the models in the testing set.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The paper states that the models were validated on a 30% test set.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.supporting_text: First, all data was split into 70% train dataset and 30% test dataset...Then, we compared each models in the training set and then validate the models in the testing set.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Whole-brain analysis for each parameter (CT, SA, and GV) to reveal the ROIs that differed between groups. The correction for multiple comparisons (Bonferroni), results were considered significant if the Bonferroni-corrected p value was ≤ 0.05.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: The study found distinct developmental trajectories of cortical morphology in ASD, identified neural biomarkers, and proposed a deep-learning model (LMFGCN) that outperforms other methods in ASD classification.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: The study found that individuals with ASD exhibit different developmental trajectories for gray matter volume, cortical thickness, and surface area compared to typically developing individuals. The LMFGCN model achieved an accuracy of 81.77% in classifying ASD. The study also identified specific brain regions with altered cortical measures in ASD.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: The study has limitations including the challenge of multi-site datasets and sex differences, the need for replication on independent datasets, and the use of cross-sectional data to infer developmental trajectories.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The authors propose a novel deep-learning workflow (LMFGCN) for ASD classification that integrates multiple types of cerebral cortical features.

general_notes.general_notes: The study provides a comprehensive analysis of brain development in ASD, combining normative modeling with a deep learning approach for classification.
